---
title: Templates
description: Start from a GitHub template or copy `.kiket/` from the in-repo flagship definition packs.
---

A template is a complete `.kiket/` directory — workflows, boards, case types, intake forms, dashboards, automations — curated for a specific kind of work. When you start a workspace *from a template*, Kiket creates a repo pre-populated with all of it.

**Prefer depth over catalog size:** for vendor onboarding, contract review, privacy/DSAR, and security incident stories, start from **[Definition packs](/docs/build/definition-packs)** (in-repo, evidence + findings + simulations). For everything else, use your own GitHub template repository or fork an existing `.kiket/` repo.

## Flagship packs (recommended)

## Using a template

<Steps>

<Step>

### Pick it at project creation

In the **New project** wizard, click **Copy from Template** and browse the gallery. Each card shows a preview of the states, case types, and integrations the template uses.

</Step>

<Step>

### Review the included workflows

Every template lists the workflows it ships. Most include one primary workflow (e.g. `contract_review`) plus one or two supporting ones (e.g. `amendment`).

</Step>

<Step>

### Create the project

Kiket creates a workspace repo from the template (via GitHub's template-repo API or a simple copy), connects it, and syncs. You land ready to create your first case.

</Step>

<Step>

### Customize in place

The template is a starting point. Edit the YAML in your IDE or the canvas in the app — both write to your repo. You're never locked to the upstream template.

</Step>

<Step>

### Add evidence sources and packs after onboarding

Install integrations from **Settings → Evidence sources** (the legacy `/marketplace` URL redirects there). To add more `.kiket/` workflows, copy from **[Definition packs](/docs/build/definition-packs)** or your own template repo into the workspace under `.kiket/`.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Forking vs. copying

Two ways to start from a template:

| Mode | Result | Use when |
|------|--------|----------|
| **Copy** (default) | Independent repo, no upstream link | You want full autonomy; the template is a starting point. |
| **Fork** | Repo forked from the upstream template | You want to pull upstream updates later. Requires the template repo to be a GitHub template. |

Copy is the right choice ~95% of the time.

## Authoring your own template

Any `.kiket/`-containing repo can be a template. To publish:

1. Mark the GitHub repo as a **template repository** (Settings → Template).
2. Add `metadata.yaml` at the repo root listing preview details (states, integrations, category).
3. Share the repo URL; anyone can use it via **From GitHub → Template URL**.
